pathway.title: Sunoco LP — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage has fallen sharply, but part of the fall is perimeter change. Sunoco LP's net debt over trailing Adjusted EBITDA fell from 6.11x at FY2025 to 3.51x at Q3 2026, and the reported covenant net leverage fell from 4.03x to 3.5x [CP-1]. The mechanism is that Parkland (acquired on 2025-10-31) contributed two months to FY2025 earnings but eleven months to the Q3 2026 trailing window while its debt was fully on the balance sheet at both dates [CP-1, CP-1A]. The implication is that headroom against the 5.50x covenant ceiling is wide on the reported basis, yet the trajectory should be judged on pro forma earnings that the sources do not supply.

Liquidity is strong against a staggered maturity profile. Sunoco LP held USD 760 million of cash and USD 2,300 million of undrawn revolver, total USD 3,060 million, at 2026-09-30, after USD 111 million drawn and USD 84 million of letters of credit [CP-1]. Maturities are USD 1,049 million in 2027, USD 900 million in 2028, USD 2,723 million in 2029 and USD 2,309 million in 2030 including the revolver [CP-1]. The 2027 notes are classified as long-term only on management's intent and ability to refinance, so the mechanism is market access rather than cash on hand. The implication is that refinancing risk is low in the next twelve months and moderate in 2027 to 2029, when USD 4,672 million falls due.

Debt service is well covered on a cash basis. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 3,535 million covers trailing cash interest of USD 726 million 4.87 times, against a covenant minimum of 2.25x that the filings do not report a figure against [CP-1]. Only USD 398 million of debt is variable-rate, so a 100 basis point rate move changes annual interest expense by about USD 4 million (Q3 10-Q page:48). The implication is limited interest-rate sensitivity; the more relevant sensitivity is operating, not financial.

Cash generation covers distributions, with timing help. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 2,251 million exceeded capital expenditure of USD 579 million and distributions of USD 880 million [CP-1]. The mechanism includes a USD 316 million working-capital inflow, a USD 102 million last-in first-out liquidation benefit to pre-tax income and a USD 94 million non-cash foreign exchange loss [CP-1]. Distribution commitments rise with the rate and unit count and include equal payments to SunocoCorp through 2027-12-31 and USD 76 million of incentive distributions for Q3 2026 [CP-1A]. The implication is that free cash flow after distributions is positive (see Calculations) but is not a stable annuity: it depends on working capital timing and fuel prices.

Earnings quality needs care. Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back USD 200 million of unconsolidated affiliate EBITDA, USD 131 million of other non-cash adjustments and removes a USD 445 million favourable inventory valuation adjustment in nine months 2026 [CP-1]. Covenant ratios use credit-agreement definitions that are not supplied [CP-0, CP-1]. The implication is that the derived ratios in this synthesis are a guide and the covenant headroom is a reported claim, not a verified result.

Structure and control weigh on creditor protection. Energy Transfer owns the general partner, 28,463,967 common units and all incentive distribution rights, and controls the board appointment right through SunocoCorp [CP-1A]. Notes are guaranteed by subsidiaries and rank effectively behind secured obligations including the revolver, and structurally behind debt of non-guarantor subsidiaries, which hold USD 11.73 billion of long-term assets (Q3 10-Q page:47); the line for lease-related financing and other subsidiary debt is USD 597 million and its obligors are not identified [CP-1]. The implication is that the capacity to pay out cash or add debt depends on indenture and partnership agreement terms that are not supplied, so legal capacity is not assessed.

Acquisition pace is the main forward risk. Four acquisitions closed within twelve months, the latest being Offen on 2026-10-27 for about USD 600 million in cash [CP-1A]. The mechanism is that purchase prices and acquired debt enter the balance sheet at once while earnings arrive gradually, and fair value work is open. An all-debt illustration would lift net leverage to about 3.68x before any Offen earnings (see Calculations). The implication is that further leverage movement depends on funding choice and integration.

runs.text: Strengths. Scale and diversification (Documentary Fact): four segments with Fuel Distribution, Pipeline Systems, Terminals and Refinery all contributing in Q3 2026, and operations in 33 countries and territories [CP-1A]. This reduces dependence on one margin source and supports revenue visibility. Fee-based and contracted income (Documentary Fact): pipeline and terminal throughput, remaining performance obligations of USD 2,038 million and a 15-year take-or-pay fuel supply agreement with minimum gross profit with the largest customer [CP-1A]. This supports cash conversion in weaker fuel-margin periods. Liquidity and maturity management (Documentary Fact): USD 3,060 million of liquidity, a revolver maturing 2030-06-17 and 2026 and 2027 notes replaced by notes due 2031 and 2034 [CP-1, CP-1A]. This lowers near-term refinancing risk. Deleveraging record (Documentary Fact): covenant net leverage reported at 4.03x, 3.98x, 3.7x and 3.5x across the last four reporting dates [CP-1]. This shows a funding and earnings path that creditors can monitor. Equity cushion (Analyst Interpretation): total equity of USD 8,512 million including USD 1,477 million of preferred units sits beneath USD 13,163 million of debt, which is 60.7% of debt plus equity (see Calculations) [CP-1]. Preferred and Class D equity were used for part of the Parkland price [CP-1A].

Weaknesses. Acquisition dependence (Documentary Fact): Parkland, TanQuid, Delta and Offen in twelve months with open fair value work [CP-1A]. This makes trailing metrics unrepresentative and exposes leverage to integration. Sponsor control and cash leakage (Documentary Fact): Energy Transfer control, incentive distributions at the top tier share and a general partner that must favour Energy Transfer's interests under its contractual duty [CP-1A]. This competes with debt reduction for cash. Commodity and single-site exposure (Analyst Interpretation): the Burnaby Refinery earned USD 238 million of Segment Adjusted EBITDA in Q3 2026, largely on intersegment sales whose pricing terms are not described [CP-1A]. This adds margin volatility. Thin per-gallon margins and working capital swings (Analyst Interpretation): fuel is most of revenue and working capital moved by USD 316 million in nine months 2026 [CP-1, CP-1A]. Customer concentration (Documentary Fact): 7-Eleven was about 13% of FY2025 revenues [CP-1A]. Disclosure limits (Insufficient Information): the indentures, credit agreement, partnership agreement, ratings and pro forma earnings are not supplied, which stops conclusions on covenant headroom, restricted payments and rating-linked pricing. Market view of the debt (Documentary Fact): the aggregate fair value of debt was USD 12.88 billion against a carrying amount of USD 13.16 billion at 2026-09-30, the reverse of the position at 2025-12-31 (Q3 10-Q page:15); the sources do not explain the move.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The defining transaction is the Parkland acquisition, completed on 2025-10-31 by Sunoco Retail LLC, a wholly owned corporate subsidiary. Parkland shareholders received 0.295 SunocoCorp units and C$19.80 in cash per Parkland share, or could elect cash or units subject to proration. The Partnership paid about 2.60 billion US$ to Parkland shareholders and transferred 51,517,198 SunocoCorp common units, which it had received in exchange for issuing 51,517,198 Class D Units to SunocoCorp (10-K page:7). Total consideration was 5,015 US$m (4,551 US$m net of cash acquired), against assumed long-term debt of 3,797 US$m, goodwill of 1,528 US$m and intangible assets of 1,871 US$m, all on a preliminary allocation (10-K page:238). The cash portion was funded in part by the September 2025 issuance of 1.00 billion US$ of 5.625% senior notes due 2031 and 900 million US$ of 5.875% senior notes due 2034, and by the 1.5 million Series A Preferred Units sold for net proceeds of about 1.47 billion US$ (10-K page:140). The Parkland senior note exchange closed on 2025-11-07 with about C$1.47 billion and 2.58 billion US$ of Parkland notes tendered, leaving 111 US$m of Parkland notes outstanding at 2025-12-31 (10-K page:140 and page:139); the Q3 10-Q shows those residual Parkland notes redeemed in 2026 (page:14). SunocoCorp was repurposed as a publicly traded corporation holding the Class D Units, and the Partnership must keep SunocoCorp distributions equal to its own through the equalisation period (Q3 10-Q page:19).

In 2026 the Partnership acquired TanQuid on 2026-01-16 (15 fuel terminals in Germany and one in Poland) for 239 US$m with 346 US$m of assumed debt at fair value, funded from cash and the revolving credit facility, and Delta on 2026-04-01 for about 81 US$m, with terminals and distribution assets in five Caribbean markets (Q3 10-Q page:9 and page:10). Purchase accounting for TanQuid is preliminary. After quarter end, on 2026-10-27, Sunoco Retail acquired Offen Petroleum, a US fuel distributor of about 2.5 billion gallons a year, for about 600 US$m in cash plus working capital; the funding source and the effect on 2026-10-31 liquidity are not stated, and fair value work is incomplete (Q3 10-Q page:10). On 2026-10-08 the receivables financing agreement was terminated with no borrowings outstanding (Q3 10-Q page:15).

New debt issued in the period: in March 2025, 1.00 billion US$ of 6.250% senior notes due 2033, used to repay 600 US$m of 5.750% notes due 2025 and part of the revolver (10-K page:140); in September 2025, the 5.625% 2031 and 5.875% 2034 notes above; in March 2026, 600 US$m of 5.375% senior notes due 2031 and 600 US$m of 5.625% senior notes due 2034, both maturing on 2031-07-15 and 2034-07-15, with part of the proceeds used to redeem the 500 US$m 6.000% notes due 2026 and the 600 US$m 6.000% notes due 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:14). Net of these redemptions the March 2026 issuance added 100 US$m of principal. Parkland's remaining notes were redeemed in March 2026, the 3.875% CAD notes due 2026 in June 2026 and the 6.000% CAD notes due 2028 in August 2026. The earlier history includes the NuStar acquisition of 2024-05-03 (about 51.5 million Sunoco common units issued, about 3.5 billion US$ of debt assumed, and NuStar preferred units, subordinated notes and credit facility repaid after closing), the sale of 204 West Texas convenience stores to 7-Eleven on 2024-04-16 for about 1.0 billion US$ with a 586 US$m gain, and the formation of the ET-S Permian joint venture with Energy Transfer on 2024-07-01 (10-K page:240 to page:242).

fields.value: The financial base is usable for a credit snapshot of the consolidated Partnership, with limitations. Reported statements for FY2025, the first nine months of 2026 and Q3 2026 are complete and internally consistent (the quarterly Adjusted EBITDA figures sum to the nine-month figure; see Calculations). Scale changed sharply because Parkland was acquired on 2025-10-31, so FY2025 contains two months of Parkland and the trailing Q3 2026 window contains eleven. The FY2025 leverage ratios are therefore overstated relative to a pro forma view, and the trailing Q3 2026 ratios are modestly overstated too. The management-reported covenant net leverage (4.03x at FY2025, 3.98x, 3.7x and 3.5x through Q3 2026) tracks the derived net ratio closely only at Q3 2026, which is consistent with the covenant definition being pro forma for acquisitions and netting reserved cash. Debt is dominated by unsecured senior notes with guarantees from subsidiaries; liquidity rests on a single 2,500 US$m revolver maturing 2030-06-17. Earnings quality needs care: Adjusted EBITDA adds back equity-affiliate EBITDA and a large non-cash adjustment, and excludes a favourable inventory valuation adjustment. None of these restricts the base, but each is carried into later modules.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt at 2026-09-30 is 13,163 US$m (carrying), made up of senior notes, the revolver, GoZone bonds, lease-related financing and other subsidiary debt, less 80 US$m of issuance costs (Q3 10-Q page:13). Issuers and guarantors, as the filing states: notes of Sunoco LP and Sunoco Finance Corp. (co-issuer) are guaranteed by NuStar Logistics and other subsidiaries; notes of NuStar Logistics are guaranteed by Sunoco LP, Sunoco Finance Corp. and subsidiaries; guarantees rank equally with other unsecured senior debt of each guarantor and are structurally subordinated to debt of non-guarantor subsidiaries (Q3 10-Q page:46 and page:47). The 10-K says the Sunoco senior notes are effectively subordinated to the issuers' and guarantors' secured obligations, including the Credit Facility, to the extent of the collateral value (10-K page:250), and that the Credit Facility is guaranteed by material domestic subsidiaries (10-K page:251); the collateral package is not described in the sources. Energy Transfer guarantees collection of the principal of the 5.875% senior notes due 2028 (10-K page:250). During 2026 the Partnership issued 600 US$m of 5.375% notes due 2031 and 600 US$m of 5.625% notes due 2034 and redeemed the 6.000% notes due 2026 and 2027, the Parkland notes not exchanged, the 3.875% CAD notes due 2026 and the 6.000% CAD notes due 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:14). Notes repaid in the nine months were 1,878 US$m against 1,200 US$m borrowed (Q3 10-Q page:5 and page:6).

fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure: operating lease liabilities of 185 US$m current and 1,375 US$m non-current (Q3 10-Q page:3); Series A Preferred Units of 1,477 US$m at a 7.875% rate with 39.375 US$ per unit paid semi-annually, which are equity and not debt (Q3 10-Q page:3 and page:20); Class D units held by SunocoCorp with distribution equalisation through 2027-12-31 (Q3 10-Q page:19); environmental liabilities of 213 US$m and asset retirement obligations of 214 US$m (Q3 10-Q page:18 and page:15 to page:16); a New York motor fuel excise tax assessment of about 20 US$m under appeal (Q3 10-Q page:18). The pension plan was terminated in 2024 and the benefit obligation was nil at 2025-12-31 (10-K page:274). Purchase commitments, factoring and supply-chain finance were searched in the 10-K and the Q3 10-Q and no such disclosure was found. Debt-like lease financing obligations are inside the 597 US$m line.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenants: the 10-K states a maximum Net Leverage Ratio of 5.50 to 1.00 before an investment grade rating and a minimum Interest Coverage Ratio of 2.25 to 1.00 (10-K page:251). The Q3 10-Q reports net leverage of 3.5 to 1.00 and compliance with all financial covenants (page:15). The reported interest coverage ratio is not printed in any source. The step-down to 5.00 to 1.00 applies only after an investment grade rating, and no rating is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Adjusted EBITDA is the Partnership's non-GAAP measure and "is used as a performance measure under our Credit Facility" (Q3 10-Q page:32). It starts at net income and adds back interest, tax, depreciation, amortisation and accretion, unit-based compensation, disposal losses and impairments, extinguishment losses, unrealised commodity derivative effects, inventory valuation adjustments, certain foreign exchange effects and other items; it adds Adjusted EBITDA of unconsolidated affiliates and subtracts their equity earnings (Q3 10-Q page:21 and page:22). For the nine months of 2026 the add-back for unconsolidated affiliates is 200 US$m, other non-cash adjustments are 131 US$m, and the inventory valuation adjustment removes 445 US$m of favourable effect (Q3 10-Q page:33). The Q3 release headline of 1.060 billion US$ excludes one-time transaction-related expenses of 11 US$m, whereas the filing and the release body show 1,049 US$m (release Q3 page:2). This handoff uses the filing figure. Differences from the covenant ratio: the covenant net leverage uses the credit-agreement Net Leverage Ratio, which after a 2025 amendment provided for up to 2.00 billion US$ of cash reserved for the Parkland consideration to be netted (10-K page:252) and is not computed from statements here.

fields.value: Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow was 2,251 US$m on net income of 1,426 US$m, with working capital contributing a 316 US$m inflow (the cash flow effect of accounts receivable was an outflow of 2,313 US$m and that of accounts payable an inflow of 1,479 US$m, Q3 10-Q page:11). The inventory valuation adjustment of 445 US$m raised net income without cash and is reversed in cash flow. A last-in first-out liquidation in the first quarter raised pre-tax income by 102 US$m (Q3 10-Q page:12). A foreign exchange loss of 94 US$m was non-cash (Q3 10-Q page:42). Acquisitions in the nine months were TanQuid (194 US$m net of cash), Delta (75 US$m) and other (87 US$m) (Q3 10-Q page:5). Distributions of 880 US$m were paid in the nine months, including 151 US$m to the Class D unitholder and 118 US$m to preferred unitholders (Q3 10-Q page:6). The distribution declared for Q3 2026 is 1.0148 US$ per common unit, payable 2026-11-19, about 139 US$m on common units, 52 US$m on Class D units and 76 US$m to incentive distribution rights (Q3 10-Q page:44). Segment Adjusted EBITDA in Q3 2026 was Fuel Distribution 523, Pipeline Systems 166, Terminals 122 and Refinery 238 US$m (Q3 10-Q page:22); the Refinery segment sells largely to other segments (intersegment revenues 853 US$m of 970 US$m in the quarter, page:22).

On 2026-10-08 the receivables financing agreement was terminated with no borrowings outstanding (page:15). On 2026-10-22 the Q3 distribution was announced (page:44). The Q3 release says the Partnership expects to exceed its 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of 3.5 billion to 3.7 billion US$ (release Q3 page:2); this is a management claim. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a four-segment energy infrastructure and fuel distribution group: Fuel Distribution, Pipeline Systems, Terminals and Refinery. It operates across 33 countries and territories in North America, the Greater Caribbean and Europe, with about 14,000 miles of pipeline, over 170 terminals and capacity to distribute over 17 billion gallons annually (Q3 10-Q page:7). The step change came from the Parkland acquisition on 2025-10-31, which added Canadian and Caribbean distribution and the Burnaby refinery, on top of the NuStar acquisition of 2024-05-03, which added pipelines and terminals. Ownership is concentrated: Energy Transfer owns the general partner, a minority of the common units and all incentive distribution rights, and through SunocoCorp controls the board appointment right. The creditor view is a larger, more diversified earnings base than before the acquisitions, financed largely with debt and preferred equity, under a sponsor whose economic interest (incentive distributions) is separate from that of the debt holders. Documented behaviour since 2024 shows continued acquisition activity paired with reported leverage reduction and rising distributions, which is mixed for creditors rather than adverse. The decisive open items are the fair-value work on Parkland, TanQuid, Delta and Offen, the funding of Offen, and the absence of the executed documents that set distribution, debt and change-of-control limits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The defining transaction is the Parkland acquisition, completed on 2025-10-31 by Sunoco Retail LLC, a wholly owned corporate subsidiary. Parkland shareholders received 0.295 SunocoCorp units and C$19.80 in cash per Parkland share, or could elect cash or units subject to proration. The Partnership paid about 2.60 billion US$ to Parkland shareholders and transferred 51,517,198 SunocoCorp common units, which it had received in exchange for issuing 51,517,198 Class D Units to SunocoCorp (10-K page:7). Total consideration was 5,015 US$m (4,551 US$m net of cash acquired), against assumed long-term debt of 3,797 US$m, goodwill of 1,528 US$m and intangible assets of 1,871 US$m, all on a preliminary allocation (10-K page:238). The cash portion was funded in part by the September 2025 issuance of 1.00 billion US$ of 5.625% senior notes due 2031 and 900 million US$ of 5.875% senior notes due 2034, and by the 1.5 million Series A Preferred Units sold for net proceeds of about 1.47 billion US$ (10-K page:140). The Parkland senior note exchange closed on 2025-11-07 with about C$1.47 billion and 2.58 billion US$ of Parkland notes tendered, leaving 111 US$m of Parkland notes outstanding at 2025-12-31 (10-K page:140 and page:139); the Q3 10-Q shows those residual Parkland notes redeemed in 2026 (page:14). SunocoCorp was repurposed as a publicly traded corporation holding the Class D Units, and the Partnership must keep SunocoCorp distributions equal to its own through the equalisation period (Q3 10-Q page:19).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In 2026 the Partnership acquired TanQuid on 2026-01-16 (15 fuel terminals in Germany and one in Poland) for 239 US$m with 346 US$m of assumed debt at fair value, funded from cash and the revolving credit facility, and Delta on 2026-04-01 for about 81 US$m, with terminals and distribution assets in five Caribbean markets (Q3 10-Q page:9 and page:10). Purchase accounting for TanQuid is preliminary. After quarter end, on 2026-10-27, Sunoco Retail acquired Offen Petroleum, a US fuel distributor of about 2.5 billion gallons a year, for about 600 US$m in cash plus working capital; the funding source and the effect on 2026-10-31 liquidity are not stated, and fair value work is incomplete (Q3 10-Q page:10). On 2026-10-08 the receivables financing agreement was terminated with no borrowings outstanding (Q3 10-Q page:15).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issued in the period: in March 2025, 1.00 billion US$ of 6.250% senior notes due 2033, used to repay 600 US$m of 5.750% notes due 2025 and part of the revolver (10-K page:140); in September 2025, the 5.625% 2031 and 5.875% 2034 notes above; in March 2026, 600 US$m of 5.375% senior notes due 2031 and 600 US$m of 5.625% senior notes due 2034, both maturing on 2031-07-15 and 2034-07-15, with part of the proceeds used to redeem the 500 US$m 6.000% notes due 2026 and the 600 US$m 6.000% notes due 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:14). Net of these redemptions the March 2026 issuance added 100 US$m of principal. Parkland's remaining notes were redeemed in March 2026, the 3.875% CAD notes due 2026 in June 2026 and the 6.000% CAD notes due 2028 in August 2026. The earlier history includes the NuStar acquisition of 2024-05-03 (about 51.5 million Sunoco common units issued, about 3.5 billion US$ of debt assumed, and NuStar preferred units, subordinated notes and credit facility repaid after closing), the sale of 204 West Texas convenience stores to 7-Eleven on 2024-04-16 for about 1.0 billion US$ with a 586 US$m gain, and the formation of the ET-S Permian joint venture with Energy Transfer on 2024-07-01 (10-K page:240 to page:242).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Energy Transfer owns 100% of the general partner membership interest, 28,463,967 common units and all incentive distribution rights, and controls SunocoCorp, which owns all Class D Units (Q3 10-Q page:7). Under a Delegation Agreement dated 2025-10-27, Energy Transfer delegated its power to elect, appoint and remove the Sunoco GP LLC board to SunocoCorp; the rights terminate on certain SunocoCorp insolvency events or at Energy Transfer's election, and the general partner agreed not to amend the partnership agreement against those rights or to withdraw while SunocoCorp is listed or not wholly owned by Energy Transfer (10-K page:197). The 10-K states that general partner officers and directors "also have a contractual duty to manage our General Partner in a manner beneficial to Energy Transfer" and that conflicts of interest may arise (10-K page:91). An Omnibus Agreement dated 2025-10-31 has the Partnership indemnify SunocoCorp, provide all general and administrative services and fund SunocoCorp's distributions equal to those on Sunoco common units through the eighth full quarter after closing (10-K page:197 and page:198).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sunoco LP is a sponsor-controlled fuel distribution and midstream credit whose leverage has fallen to about 3.5x and whose liquidity is ample. Its strongest support is scale and diversification: trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 3,535 million across four segments, net debt of 3.51x that figure, and liquidity of USD 3,060 million against USD 1,049 million of notes due in 2027. The weakest point is that the improvement rests on recently acquired earnings, management-adjusted EBITDA and a sponsor whose incentive distributions and board control sit beside creditor interests, while funding for the USD 600 million Offen purchase is not described. Whether Parkland integration and refinery margins keep earnings at this level decides whether leverage keeps falling.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has fallen sharply, but part of the fall is perimeter change. Sunoco LP's net debt over trailing Adjusted EBITDA fell from 6.11x at FY2025 to 3.51x at Q3 2026, and the reported covenant net leverage fell from 4.03x to 3.5x [CP-1]. The mechanism is that Parkland (acquired on 2025-10-31) contributed two months to FY2025 earnings but eleven months to the Q3 2026 trailing window while its debt was fully on the balance sheet at both dates [CP-1, CP-1A]. The implication is that headroom against the 5.50x covenant ceiling is wide on the reported basis, yet the trajectory should be judged on pro forma earnings that the sources do not supply.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is strong against a staggered maturity profile. Sunoco LP held USD 760 million of cash and USD 2,300 million of undrawn revolver, total USD 3,060 million, at 2026-09-30, after USD 111 million drawn and USD 84 million of letters of credit [CP-1]. Maturities are USD 1,049 million in 2027, USD 900 million in 2028, USD 2,723 million in 2029 and USD 2,309 million in 2030 including the revolver [CP-1]. The 2027 notes are classified as long-term only on management's intent and ability to refinance, so the mechanism is market access rather than cash on hand. The implication is that refinancing risk is low in the next twelve months and moderate in 2027 to 2029, when USD 4,672 million falls due.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt service is well covered on a cash basis. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 3,535 million covers trailing cash interest of USD 726 million 4.87 times, against a covenant minimum of 2.25x that the filings do not report a figure against [CP-1]. Only USD 398 million of debt is variable-rate, so a 100 basis point rate move changes annual interest expense by about USD 4 million (Q3 10-Q page:48). The implication is limited interest-rate sensitivity; the more relevant sensitivity is operating, not financial.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation covers distributions, with timing help. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 2,251 million exceeded capital expenditure of USD 579 million and distributions of USD 880 million [CP-1]. The mechanism includes a USD 316 million working-capital inflow, a USD 102 million last-in first-out liquidation benefit to pre-tax income and a USD 94 million non-cash foreign exchange loss [CP-1]. Distribution commitments rise with the rate and unit count and include equal payments to SunocoCorp through 2027-12-31 and USD 76 million of incentive distributions for Q3 2026 [CP-1A]. The implication is that free cash flow after distributions is positive (see Calculations) but is not a stable annuity: it depends on working capital timing and fuel prices.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality needs care. Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back USD 200 million of unconsolidated affiliate EBITDA, USD 131 million of other non-cash adjustments and removes a USD 445 million favourable inventory valuation adjustment in nine months 2026 [CP-1]. Covenant ratios use credit-agreement definitions that are not supplied [CP-0, CP-1]. The implication is that the derived ratios in this synthesis are a guide and the covenant headroom is a reported claim, not a verified result.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Structure and control weigh on creditor protection. Energy Transfer owns the general partner, 28,463,967 common units and all incentive distribution rights, and controls the board appointment right through SunocoCorp [CP-1A]. Notes are guaranteed by subsidiaries and rank effectively behind secured obligations including the revolver, and structurally behind debt of non-guarantor subsidiaries, which hold USD 11.73 billion of long-term assets (Q3 10-Q page:47); the line for lease-related financing and other subsidiary debt is USD 597 million and its obligors are not identified [CP-1]. The implication is that the capacity to pay out cash or add debt depends on indenture and partnership agreement terms that are not supplied, so legal capacity is not assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisition pace is the main forward risk. Four acquisitions closed within twelve months, the latest being Offen on 2026-10-27 for about USD 600 million in cash [CP-1A]. The mechanism is that purchase prices and acquired debt enter the balance sheet at once while earnings arrive gradually, and fair value work is open. An all-debt illustration would lift net leverage to about 3.68x before any Offen earnings (see Calculations). The implication is that further leverage movement depends on funding choice and integration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Scale and diversification (Documentary Fact): four segments with Fuel Distribution, Pipeline Systems, Terminals and Refinery all contributing in Q3 2026, and operations in 33 countries and territories [CP-1A]. This reduces dependence on one margin source and supports revenue visibility. Fee-based and contracted income (Documentary Fact): pipeline and terminal throughput, remaining performance obligations of USD 2,038 million and a 15-year take-or-pay fuel supply agreement with minimum gross profit with the largest customer [CP-1A]. This supports cash conversion in weaker fuel-margin periods. Liquidity and maturity management (Documentary Fact): USD 3,060 million of liquidity, a revolver maturing 2030-06-17 and 2026 and 2027 notes replaced by notes due 2031 and 2034 [CP-1, CP-1A]. This lowers near-term refinancing risk. Deleveraging record (Documentary Fact): covenant net leverage reported at 4.03x, 3.98x, 3.7x and 3.5x across the last four reporting dates [CP-1]. This shows a funding and earnings path that creditors can monitor. Equity cushion (Analyst Interpretation): total equity of USD 8,512 million including USD 1,477 million of preferred units sits beneath USD 13,163 million of debt, which is 60.7% of debt plus equity (see Calculations) [CP-1]. Preferred and Class D equity were used for part of the Parkland price [CP-1A].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Acquisition dependence (Documentary Fact): Parkland, TanQuid, Delta and Offen in twelve months with open fair value work [CP-1A]. This makes trailing metrics unrepresentative and exposes leverage to integration. Sponsor control and cash leakage (Documentary Fact): Energy Transfer control, incentive distributions at the top tier share and a general partner that must favour Energy Transfer's interests under its contractual duty [CP-1A]. This competes with debt reduction for cash. Commodity and single-site exposure (Analyst Interpretation): the Burnaby Refinery earned USD 238 million of Segment Adjusted EBITDA in Q3 2026, largely on intersegment sales whose pricing terms are not described [CP-1A]. This adds margin volatility. Thin per-gallon margins and working capital swings (Analyst Interpretation): fuel is most of revenue and working capital moved by USD 316 million in nine months 2026 [CP-1, CP-1A]. Customer concentration (Documentary Fact): 7-Eleven was about 13% of FY2025 revenues [CP-1A]. Disclosure limits (Insufficient Information): the indentures, credit agreement, partnership agreement, ratings and pro forma earnings are not supplied, which stops conclusions on covenant headroom, restricted payments and rating-linked pricing. Market view of the debt (Documentary Fact): the aggregate fair value of debt was USD 12.88 billion against a carrying amount of USD 13.16 billion at 2026-09-30, the reverse of the position at 2025-12-31 (Q3 10-Q page:15); the sources do not explain the move.
